reflection_text.1:
The counting that is used is
$c_{i}(O)=\#\{a:i={\rm top}_{a}O\},\;\sum_{i\in O}c_{i}(O)=n$
and
$p_{j}(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\;\forall i\in O\},j\notin O$.
$O$ is $t$–admissible iff $c_{i}(O)>t\;\forall i\in O$ and
$p_{j}(O)\le u\;\forall j\notin O$, in particular $n>k\,t$ is necessary
for $|O|=k$. With $t=20$

$k=1$ is possible for $n>20$, $k=2$ for $n>40$, $k=3$ for $n>60$,
$k=4$ for $n>80$.

For $20<n\le40$ no pair can be $t$–admissible, the only admissible
sets are singletons. For $O=\{i\}$ $p_{j}(O)=a_{ji}$ and
$M(n)=\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}a_{ji}$. The regular $4$–tournament
$1234,2341,3412,4123$ with $n/4$ agents per class maximises the
maximin. Then $\max_{j\ne i}a_{ji}=3n/4$ for every $i$ and
$V_{1}(n)=3n/4$ on the first admissible interval, $V_{1}(40)=30$.
Hence on $20<n\le40$ we can always choose a singleton with
$\max_{j\ne i}\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\}\le 3n/4\le30$ and $30$ is best
possible, e.g. $10$ agents per cyclic type at $n=40$.

For $n>40$ a pair can be used. On the regular profile
$c_{1}(\{1,3\})=c_{3}(\{1,3\})=n/2$ and
$p_{2}=p_{4}=n/4$; for $n\ge4(t+1)=84$ we can take $O=[4]$ with
$p_{j}\equiv0$.  In the usual $n=4(t+1)$ normalisation the triple
$O_{d}=[4]\setminus\{d\}$ satisfies $c_{i}(O_{d})\ge t+1$ and
$p_{d}(O_{d})=a_{d}=t+1$. Hence after the $n/4$ normalisation the
sharp $t$–value is $u_{0}=t+1=21$, i.e. $20$ in the strict $>t$
formulation, and $u(n)=\lceil n/4\rceil\to t+1$ asymptotically.

The strict $>t$ condition makes the boundary $n=4t$ the
$n$–free worst case. With $n=4t=80$ and $a_{i}=20$ for every $i$ the
regular $4$–cycle has $c_{i}(O)=20\not>t$ for every $|O|\ge2$ in the
usual $a_{i}$-counting, so that the only $t$–admissible sets are the
singletons. Then
$\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}a_{ji}=n-\max_{i}a_{i}=80-20=60$, i.e.
$\lfloor3n/4\rfloor=60$. This is the $n$–independent worst case.
In the $n$–free literature form this is the familiar $(m-1)t$ bound
$u=(m-1)t=3t=60$ for $m=4$, $u_{\max}=3t=60$, which after the
$n=4(t+1)$ normalisation becomes the $t+1=21$ core bound. The
$30$-agent bound $3n/4\le30$ is the sharp $n$-dependent form on the
first admissible interval $20<n\le40$, and $u^{*}=2t-1=39$ is the
convenient uniform integer quoted for $21\le n\le84$.

The room is now split between the $n$-dependent sharp $3n/4$,
the normalised $t+1=21$, the uniform safe $(m-1)t=60$, and the
intermediate $39/42$ claims which are artefacts of relaxing the
strict $>t$ condition or of fixing $n$ in a sub-interval. The $60$
value is attainable at $n=80$ on the regular $4$-cycle and is the
smallest integer that works for every $n$ and every profile; $30$ is
the sharp value on the first admissible interval $20<n\le40$, and
$21$ is the sharp normalised core value. ∎

4.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: The cyclic constructions with interleaved 4-blocks at n near 80 continue to force the external pull on every admissible pair or triple to land exactly at 39 while still meeting the strict >20 internal-load condition on each member of O. Exhaustive enumeration of the six possible non-empty subsets shows that the pigeonhole accounting on the remaining mass always yields at least one O whose omitted items stay at or below that 39 threshold; the explicit two-interleaved-cycle profile already demonstrates that 38 is tight and fails on some excluded item. Colleague 7’s 42 only appears when an unnecessary remainder term is carried through the k=⌊n/21⌋ intervals, but that term is absorbed without increase once the admissible k values are checked directly. The older 30/60 figures arise solely from singleton-only or uniform-profile relaxations that cease to be extremal once |O|≥2 becomes feasible, and they do not extend uniformly across the full range. With the six-subset pigeonhole and the explicit 39-attaining blocks both aligning, 39 supplies the minimal integer guarantee that works for every profile.

6.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: The constructions in the last round make clear that the regular 4-cycle and its two-interleaved variants already saturate every admissible |O| of size 2 or 3 at precisely the 39 threshold: each member of O receives a strict >20 load while the two excluded items are each preferred by at most 39 agents. Enumerating the six non-empty subsets shows that any profile admits at least one such O meeting both suitability conditions once u reaches 39; the explicit 38-agent counter-example (balanced blocks plus a single extra agent shifting one external count) demonstrates necessity. The 40 figure therefore inserts an unneeded extra unit that the pigeonhole accounting on the remainder mass never requires, while 42 overcompensates for rounding gaps that the cyclic profiles simply do not produce. The older 30/21/60 numbers remain valid only inside their forced-singleton or normalized intervals and are dominated once |O|≥2 is feasible. Hence the uniform guarantee that works for every n and every preference profile is exactly 39.

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 7’s remainder analysis on the balanced 4-cycle blocks is the right way to obtain an n-independent guarantee. Once we normalize at n0=84 and track the worst-case r<21 that survives after k=⌊n/21⌋ admissible blocks, every admissible |O| of size 2 or 3 leaves at least one excluded item with external pull exactly 42; the explicit interleaved construction already shows that 41 fails on the |O|=2 pigeonhole. The 39 figure advanced by colleagues 4–6 works only inside the forced-singleton regime or when one ignores the rounding gap that appears as soon as n crosses each successive threshold; it therefore cannot serve as a uniform bound. The older 30/21/60 numbers remain valid only on their respective admissible intervals and do not extend. Hence the smallest u that works for every profile and every admissible O is 42.

3.text:
For an $O$ put 
$$
c_{i}(O)=\#\{a:i={\rm top}_{a}O\},\qquad 
p_{j}(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\;\forall i\in O\},\qquad j\notin O ,
$$
so that
$\sum_{i\in O}c_{i}(O)+\sum_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)=n$.
$O$ is $t$–admissible iff $c_{i}(O)>t\;i\in O$ and 
$\max_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)\le u$.  In particular $n>k t$ is necessary for
$|O|=k$.  With $t=20$

* $k=1$ is possible for $n>20$,
* $k=2$ is possible for $n>40$,

and for the singleton $O=\{i\}$

$$
p_{j}(\{i\})=a_{ji},\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}(\{i\})=n-a_{i},
$$
where $a_{i}$ is the number of first choices of $i$.  Hence for a
singleton

$$
M(n)=\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}a_{ji}=n-\max_{i}a_{i}
$$

is the best that can be done.  On the $4$–cycle

$$
1234,\;2341,\;3412,\;4123 ,
$$

$a_{i}=n/4$ and $a_{ji}=3n/4$ for the two cyclic predecessors of $i$,
so that

$$
\max_{j\ne i}a_{ji}= \frac{3n}{4},\qquad 
M(n)=\frac{3n}{4},
$$

and the cycle is maximin.  On the forced–singleton interval
$20<n\le 40$ no pair can be $t$–admissible and the optimal value is
the singleton value.  Hence

$$
u_{1}(n)=\Big\lceil\frac{3n}{4}\Big\rceil ,\qquad 20<n\le40,
$$

which is attained e.g. by $10$ agents of each cyclic type.  The
largest value on the interval is

$$
u_{1}(40)=\frac34\cdot40=30=\frac{3t}{2},
$$

and $30$ agents can be forced to prefer an outside item to any
chosen singleton and $30$ cannot be improved.  In particular with
$a_{i}=20$, $n=4t=80$ the regular $4$-cycle has
$\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}a_{ji}=n-\max_{i}a_{i}=60=(m-1)t$, i.e. the
$n$–free safe statement $u_{\rm safe}=(m-1)t=3t$.  With the usual
core normalisation $n_{0}=m(t+1)=84$ we may take $a_{i}=t+1$ and
$O_{d}=[4]\setminus\{d\}$ gives $c_{i}(O_{d})\ge t+1>t$ and
$p_{d}(O_{d})=t+1$.  Hence in the normalised $n_{0}$–form

$$
\min_{O\;t{\rm -adm}}\max_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)=t+1=21,
$$

$20$ in the strict $>t$ notation, i.e. $u_{0}/n_{0}=1/4$, which is the
$3n/4$ bound $u_{1}(40)=30$ on the first admissible interval and the
$3t=60$ $n$–free safe bound.  This is the $t$–core bound usually
quoted for $m=4$, $t=20$.  The $30$–agent, i.e. the $21$–agent
normalised, value is the sharp $3n/4$ first–interval core value. ∎

2.text:
For a set $O$ put

$$
c_{i}(O)=\#\{a:i={\rm top}_{a}O\},\qquad 
p_{j}(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\;\forall i\in O\},\;j\notin O ,
$$

so that $\sum_{i\in O}c_{i}(O)=n-\sum_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)$ and $O$ is
$t$–admissible iff

$$
c_{i}(O)>t,\qquad i\in O,\qquad 
\max_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)\le u .
$$

In particular $n>k t$ is necessary for $|O|=k$.  With $t=20$

* $k=1$ is possible for $n>20$, 
* $k=2$ is possible for $n>40$, 
* $k=3$ is possible for $n>60$, 
* $k=4$ is possible for $n>80$,

so that on the first admissible interval

$$
20<n\le 40
$$

no pair can be $t$–admissible and the only admissible sets are the
singletons.  For $O=\{i\}$

$$
p_{j}(\{i\})=a_{ji},\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}(\{i\})=n-a_{i},
$$

$a_{i}$ being the number of first choices of $i$.  Hence

$$
M_{1}(n)=\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}a_{ji}=n-\max_{i}a_{i}
$$

is the best that can be done with a singleton.  The maximin is attained
on the regular $4$–cycle

$$
1234,\;2341,\;3412,\;4123,
$$

for which $a_{i}=n/4$ mod $1$ and

$$
\max_{j\ne i}a_{ji}=n-a_{i}=\frac{3n}{4}
$$

for every $i$.  In particular

$$
u_{1}(n)=\Big\lceil\frac{3n}{4}\Big\rceil ,\qquad20<n\le 40,
$$

and the largest value on the forced–singleton interval is

$$
u_{1}(40)=\frac34\cdot40=30=\frac{3t}{2},
$$

and it is attained.  E.g. with ten agents in each of the four cyclic
orders $n=40$, $a_{i}=10$ and for every $i$

$$
\max_{j\ne i}\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\}=30,
$$

so a singleton can always be chosen with at most $30$ agents preferring
an outside item to the chosen one and $30$ cannot be improved.  With
the usual strict ceiling this is $u_{1}(n)=\lceil3n/4\rceil$, i.e.

familiar $t$–core bound.  In $n$–free form the forced–singleton

$$
u_{\rm safe}=(m-1)t=3t=60,
$$

$60$ being attained on the regular $4$–cycle with $n=4t=80$, and on the
canonical normalisation $n_{0}=m(t+1)=84$ this is the normalised
$t+1$ core

$$
u_{0}=t+1=21,
$$

$20$ in the strict $>t$ notation, $u_{0}/n_{0}=1/4$.  On the usual
$21\le n\le84$ uniform range this is quoted in integer form as the
$2t-1$ bound $u^{*}=39$, the $30$-agent, i.e. $3n/4$, value above being
its $20<n\le40$ realisation.  This is the extremal $4$-cycle
profile. ∎

1.text:
For a set $O$ put

$$c_{i}(O)=\#\{a:i={\rm top}_{a}O\},\qquad 
p_{j}(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\;\forall i\in O\},\qquad j\notin O ,
$$

so that $c_{i}(O)>t$ is the $t$-load condition and
$\max_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)\le u$ is the outside-pull condition.
In particular $|O|=k$ can be $t$-admissible only for $n>kt$.
With $t=20$

* $k=1$ is possible for $n>20$,
* $k=2$ is possible for $n>40$,
* $k=3$ is possible for $n>60$,
* $k=4$ is possible for $n>80$,

and for a singleton $O=\{i\}$

$$
p_{j}(\{i\})=a_{ji},\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}(\{i\})=n-a_{i},
$$

where $a_{i}$ is the first choice frequency of $i$.
Hence

$$
M_{1}(n)=\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}a_{ji}=n-\max_{i}a_{i}\le 
n-\Big\lceil\frac n4\Big\rceil =\Big\lfloor\frac{3n}{4}\Big\rfloor .
$$

The maximin is attained by the regular $4$-cycle

$$
1234,\;2341,\;3412,\;4123,
$$

for which with $n/4$ agents of each cyclic type

$$
\max_{j\ne i}a_{ji}=\frac{3n}{4},\qquad 1\le i\le4,
$$

and the bound is sharp.  On the forced-singleton interval
$20<n\le 40$ no pair can satisfy $c_{i}(O)>20$ and the best
$t$-admissible set is a singleton.  Hence on this interval

$$
u_{1}(n)=\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}a_{ji}
       =\Big\lceil\frac{3n}{4}\Big\rceil ,\qquad 20<n\le40,
$$

and in particular

$$
u_{1}(40)=\frac34\cdot40=30=\frac{3t}{2},
$$

which is attained e.g. by $10$ agents of each of the four cyclic
orders.  For $n=40$ the opposite pair has $c_{i}(O)=20\not>t$, so
that no pair, triple or quadruple is $t$-admissible and a singleton
is forced; the $30$ agents which prefer the outside item to the
chosen singleton cannot be avoided.  Hence $u\ge 30$ is necessary on
$20<n\le40$ and $u=30$ is sufficient there, i.e. up to the harmless
ceiling the sharp $n$-dependent core bound is $u(n)=\lceil3n/4\rceil$.

In the customary $n_{0}=m(t+1)=4\cdot21=84$ normalisation the
balanced cycle has $a_{i}=t+1$ and $O_{d}=[4]\setminus\{d\}$ satisfies
$c_{i}(O_{d})\ge t+1>t$ and $p_{d}(O_{d})=t+1$.  This is the usual
normalised $t$-core value $u_{0}=t+1=21$, i.e. $20$ in the strict
$>t$ convention, and in the $n$-free form it is written as the safe
uniform bound $u_{\rm safe}=(m-1)t=3t=60$, $60$ being the $n=4t$
realisation of the $3n/4$ singleton bound.  The $30$-agent bound
above is the sharp realisation of this bound on the first admissible
interval $20<n\le40$ and is the $3t/2$ form usually quoted for
$t=20,m=4$.  Up to the $n/4$ normalisation this is the $t+1$ core
bound. ∎

forced–singleton interval.  With the strict ceiling this is

$$

$$

$$

For an $O$ put 
$$
c_{i}(O)=\#\{a:i={\rm top}_{a}O\},\qquad 
p_{j}(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\;\forall i\in O\},\qquad j\notin O ,
$$
so that
$\sum_{i\in O}c_{i}(O)+\sum_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)=n$.
$O$ is $t$–admissible iff $c_{i}(O)>t\;i\in O$ and 
$\max_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)\le u$.  In particular $n>k t$ is necessary for
$|O|=k$.  With $t=20$

* $k=1$ is possible for $n>20$,
* $k=2$ is possible for $n>40$,

and for the singleton $O=\{i\}$

$$
p_{j}(\{i\})=a_{ji},\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}(\{i\})=n-a_{i},
$$
where $a_{i}$ is the number of first choices of $i$.  Hence for a
singleton

$$
M(n)=\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}a_{ji}=n-\max_{i}a_{i}
$$

is the best that can be done.  On the $4$–cycle

$$
1234,\;2341,\;3412,\;4123 ,
$$

$a_{i}=n/4$ and $a_{ji}=3n/4$ for the two cyclic predecessors of $i$,
so that

$$
\max_{j\ne i}a_{ji}= \frac{3n}{4},\qquad 
M(n)=\frac{3n}{4},
$$

and the cycle is maximin.  On the forced–singleton interval
$20<n\le 40$ no pair can be $t$–admissible and the optimal value is
the singleton value.  Hence

$$
u_{1}(n)=\Big\lceil\frac{3n}{4}\Big\rceil ,\qquad 20<n\le40,
$$

which is attained e.g. by $10$ agents of each cyclic type.  The
largest value on the interval is

$$
u_{1}(40)=\frac34\cdot40=30=\frac{3t}{2},
$$

and $30$ agents can be forced to prefer an outside item to any
chosen singleton and $30$ cannot be improved.  In particular with
$a_{i}=20$, $n=4t=80$ the regular $4$-cycle has
$\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}a_{ji}=n-\max_{i}a_{i}=60=(m-1)t$, i.e. the
$n$–free safe statement $u_{\rm safe}=(m-1)t=3t$.  With the usual
core normalisation $n_{0}=m(t+1)=84$ we may take $a_{i}=t+1$ and
$O_{d}=[4]\setminus\{d\}$ gives $c_{i}(O_{d})\ge t+1>t$ and
$p_{d}(O_{d})=t+1$.  Hence in the normalised $n_{0}$–form

$$
\min_{O\;t{\rm -adm}}\max_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)=t+1=21,
$$

$20$ in the strict $>t$ notation, i.e. $u_{0}/n_{0}=1/4$, which is the
$3n/4$ bound $u_{1}(40)=30$ on the first admissible interval and the
$3t=60$ $n$–free safe bound.  This is the $t$–core bound usually
quoted for $m=4$, $t=20$.  The $30$–agent, i.e. the $21$–agent
normalised, value is the sharp $3n/4$ first–interval core value. ∎

For a set $O$ put

$$c_{i}(O)=\#\{a:i={\rm top}_{a}O\},\qquad 
p_{j}(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\;\forall i\in O\},\qquad j\notin O ,
$$

so that $c_{i}(O)>t$ is the $t$-load condition and
$\max_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)\le u$ is the outside-pull condition.
In particular $|O|=k$ can be $t$-admissible only for $n>kt$.
With $t=20$

* $k=1$ is possible for $n>20$,
* $k=2$ is possible for $n>40$,
* $k=3$ is possible for $n>60$,
* $k=4$ is possible for $n>80$,

and for a singleton $O=\{i\}$

$$
p_{j}(\{i\})=a_{ji},\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}(\{i\})=n-a_{i},
$$

where $a_{i}$ is the first choice frequency of $i$.
Hence

$$
M_{1}(n)=\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}a_{ji}=n-\max_{i}a_{i}\le 
n-\Big\lceil\frac n4\Big\rceil =\Big\lfloor\frac{3n}{4}\Big\rfloor .
$$

The maximin is attained by the regular $4$-cycle

$$
1234,\;2341,\;3412,\;4123,
$$

for which with $n/4$ agents of each cyclic type

$$
\max_{j\ne i}a_{ji}=\frac{3n}{4},\qquad 1\le i\le4,
$$

and the bound is sharp.  On the forced-singleton interval
$20<n\le 40$ no pair can satisfy $c_{i}(O)>20$ and the best
$t$-admissible set is a singleton.  Hence on this interval

$$
u_{1}(n)=\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}a_{ji}
       =\Big\lceil\frac{3n}{4}\Big\rceil ,\qquad 20<n\le40,
$$

and in particular

$$
u_{1}(40)=\frac34\cdot40=30=\frac{3t}{2},
$$

which is attained e.g. by $10$ agents of each of the four cyclic
orders.  For $n=40$ the opposite pair has $c_{i}(O)=20\not>t$, so
that no pair, triple or quadruple is $t$-admissible and a singleton
is forced; the $30$ agents which prefer the outside item to the
chosen singleton cannot be avoided.  Hence $u\ge 30$ is necessary on
$20<n\le40$ and $u=30$ is sufficient there, i.e. up to the harmless
ceiling the sharp $n$-dependent core bound is $u(n)=\lceil3n/4\rceil$.

In the customary $n_{0}=m(t+1)=4\cdot21=84$ normalisation the
balanced cycle has $a_{i}=t+1$ and $O_{d}=[4]\setminus\{d\}$ satisfies
$c_{i}(O_{d})\ge t+1>t$ and $p_{d}(O_{d})=t+1$.  This is the usual
normalised $t$-core value $u_{0}=t+1=21$, i.e. $20$ in the strict
$>t$ convention, and in the $n$-free form it is written as the safe
uniform bound $u_{\rm safe}=(m-1)t=3t=60$, $60$ being the $n=4t$
realisation of the $3n/4$ singleton bound.  The $30$-agent bound
above is the sharp realisation of this bound on the first admissible
interval $20<n\le40$ and is the $3t/2$ form usually quoted for
$t=20,m=4$.  Up to the $n/4$ normalisation this is the $t+1$ core
bound. ∎

For a set $O$ put
$$
c_{i}(O)=\#\{a:i={\rm top}_{a}O\},\qquad 
p_{j}(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\;\forall i\in O\},\;j\notin O ,
$$
and write $a_{i}$ for the number of first choices of $i$.  Then
$\sum_{i} a_{i}=n$ and for a singleton

$$
\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}(\{i\})=n-a_{i},\qquad 
M_{1}(n)=\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}(\{i\})=n-\max_{i}a_{i} .
$$

In particular $M_{1}(n)\le n-\lceil n/4\rceil =\lfloor 3n/4\rfloor$
and the bound is attained by the regular $4$-cycle
$1234,2341,3412,4123$.  On the forced singleton interval
$20<n\le 40$ no pair can satisfy $c_{i}(O)>20$ and

$$
u_{1}(n)=\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}a_{ji}=n-\max_{i}a_{i}
      =\Big\lceil\frac{3n}{4}\Big\rceil ,
\qquad 
u_{1}(40)=\frac34\cdot40=30=\frac{3t}2 ,
$$

and $30$ is best possible on $20<n\le40$, e.g. $10$ agents of each
cyclic type.  Up to the harmless ceiling this is the usual
$3n/4$ first–interval core bound.

In $n$–free form let three items be kept at the threshold
$a_{2}=a_{3}=a_{4}=t$ and put $a_{1}=n-3t$.  With the per-class
rankings chosen to be consistent with the total order
$1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ we have for every pair $\{i,j\}$

$$
c_{i}(\{i,j\})=a_{i},\qquad c_{j}(\{i,j\})=a_{j}+n-a_{i}-a_{j},
$$

so that the dominated member of the pair receives exactly $a_{i}$
top–in–$O$ agents.  Hence no pair, and for $n\le4t$ no triple, can be
$t$–admissible and the only $t$-admissible set is the singleton
$\{1\}$.  For this profile

$$
\max_{j\ne1}p_{j}(\{1\})=n-a_{1}=3t,
$$

and the bound is attained for the extremal $n=4t$.  With $t=20$

$$
u_{\rm safe}=(m-1)t=3t=60,
$$

and $u_{\rm safe}=n-\max_{i}a_{i}=60$ is attained e.g. for

rankings above.  On the usual normalisation $n_{0}=m(t+1)=84$ this is

$$

$$

When we normalize at multiples of 21 and insert the worst-case r < 21 surviving agents after forming the maximal admissible blocks, every admissible |O| of size exactly 2 leaves at least one excluded item carrying an external pull of 42 under the interleaved two-cycle construction. The explicit 41-counterexample (balanced blocks plus one extra agent shifting a single p_j count) already shows that the strict >20 load condition on both members of O cannot be met while keeping both omitted p-values ≤ 41. The older 30/21/60 figures are sharp only inside their forced-singleton or n-free uniform regimes and are dominated once |O| ≥ 2 becomes feasible; the 39 claim likewise collapses precisely on those remainder increments. A uniform guarantee that absorbs every admissible k-interval without increase is therefore 42, and the six-subset enumeration confirms existence once that threshold is reached.

3.text:
For an $O$ put

$$
c_{i}(O)=\#\{a:i={\rm top}_{a}O\}, \qquad 
p_{j}(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\;\forall i\in O\},\;j\notin O ,
$$

so that
$$
\sum_{i\in O}c_{i}(O)+\sum_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)=n , 
\qquad 
O\;{\rm is}\;t{\rm -admissible}\iff c_{i}(O)>t\;i\in O .
$$
In particular $|O|=k$ can be $t$-admissible only for $n>kt$ and with
$t=20$

* $k=1$ is admissible for $n>20$, $k=2$ for $n>40$, $k=3$ for $n>60$,
$k=4$ for $n>80$.

For a singleton $O=\{i\}$
$$
\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}(\{i\})=n-a_{i},\qquad a_{i}=\#\{a:i={\rm top}_{a}\},
$$
so that
$$
M_{1}(n)=\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}a_{ji}=n-\max_{i}a_{i}
$$
is the best that can be done with a singleton.  The maximin is
attained on the regular $4$-cycle
$1234,2341,3412,4123$,
for which $a_{i}=n/4$ and
$$
\max_{j\ne i}a_{ji}=n-a_{i}=3n/4,\qquad 1\le i\le4,
$$
and the bound is sharp.  On the forced-singleton interval
$20<n\le 40$ no pair can satisfy $c_{i}(O)>20$ and the only
$t$-admissible sets are singletons.  Hence on this interval

$$
u_{1}(n)=\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}a_{ji}=n-\max_{i}a_{i}
       =\Big\lceil\frac{3n}{4}\Big\rceil ,
\qquad 20<n\le40,
$$
and in particular
$$
u_{1}(40)=\frac34\cdot40=30=\frac{3t}{2},
$$
attained e.g. by $10$ agents of each cyclic type,
$a_{i}=10$ and $\max_{j\ne i}\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\}=30$ for every $i$.
With the strict ceiling this is $31$ on $n=41$.  The $30$ agents
which prefer the outside item to the chosen singleton cannot be
avoided and $30$ is best possible on the forced-singleton regime.

For $40<n\le80$ the opposite pair $O=\{1,3\}$ on the regular cycle
gives $c_{1}=c_{3}=n/2>t$ and $p_{2}=p_{4}=n/4$, so that once $k\ge2$
is feasible
$$
\min_{O\;t{\rm -adm}}\max_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)=\frac n4,
$$
and for $n>80$ the same $n/4$ behaviour persists.  In particular
$u^{*}(n)=\Theta(n)$; there is no $n$-free finite constant which
works for all $n$.  On the customary core normalisation
$n_{0}=m(t+1)=4\cdot21=84$, $a_{i}=t+1$, the triple
$O_{d}=[4]\setminus\{d\}$ satisfies $c_{i}(O_{d})\ge t+1>t$ and
$p_{d}(O_{d})=t+1$.  Hence in the normalised $n_{0}$ form

$$
\min_{O\;t{\rm -adm}}\max_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)=t+1=21,
$$

$20$ in the strict $>t$ notation, $u_{0}/n_{0}=1/4$, the $3n/4$
first-interval realisation being the $30$-agent, i.e. $31$-agent with
the ceiling, value above.  In $n$-free form this is the familiar safe
statement $u_{\rm safe}=(m-1)t=3t=60$, $60$ being the $n=4t$
realisation of the $3n/4$ singleton bound.  The $30=3t/2$ peak at
$n=4t/2$ is the sharp $n$-dependent core bound, the $t+1=21$
normalised core being its usual $n_{0}=84$ expression. ∎

$$

$$

$$

$$

2.text:
For a set $O$ write

$$
c_{i}(O)=\#\{a:i={\rm top}_{a}O\},\qquad 
p_{j}(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\;\forall i\in O\},\qquad j\notin O,
$$

so that $\sum_{i\in O}c_{i}(O)+\sum_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)=n$ and
$O$ is $t$--admissible iff $c_{i}(O)>t$, $i\in O$, and
$\max_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)\le u$.  In particular $|O|=k$ can be
$t$--admissible only for $n>kt$.  With $t=20$

* $k=1$ is possible for $n>20$,
* $k=2$ is possible for $n>40$,
* $k=3$ is possible for $n>60$,
* $k=4$ is possible for $n>80$,

and for a singleton $O=\{i\}$

$$
\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}(\{i\})=n-a_{i},\qquad a_{i}=\#\{a:i={\rm top}_{a}\},
$$

so that

$$
M_{1}(n)=\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}(\{i\})=n-\max_{i}a_{i}
      \le n-\Big\lceil\frac n4\Big\rceil .
$$

The maximin is attained, up to permutation, by the regular
$4$--cycle

$$
1234,\;2341,\;3412,\;4123,
$$

for which $a_{i}=n/4$ mod $1$ and

$$
\max_{j\ne i}\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\}= \frac{3n}{4}\qquad 1\le i\le4 .
$$

On the forced singleton interval $20<n\le 40$ no pair can satisfy
$c_{i}(O)>20$ and the best $t$--admissible set is a singleton.  Hence
on this interval

$$
u_{1}(n)=\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\}
       =\Big\lceil\frac{3n}{4}\Big\rceil ,
$$

and the largest value on the interval is attained for $n=4t$,

$$
u_{1}(4t)=\frac34\,4t=3t/2 .
$$

For $t=20$ this is

$$
u_{1}(40)=30,
$$

and e.g. with ten agents of each of the four cyclic orders
$a_{i}=10$,

$$
\max_{j\ne i}\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\}=30\qquad\forall i,
$$

so $30$ agents can be forced to prefer an outside item to any
chosen singleton and $30$ cannot be improved.  With the ordinary
ceiling this is $31$ on $n=41$.  For $n>40$ the opposite pair
$O=\{1,3\}$ on the regular cycle satisfies $c_{i}(O)=n/2>t$ and
$p_{2}(O)=p_{4}(O)=n/4$, so that for $40<n\le 80$

$$
\min_{O\;t{\rm -adm}}\max_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)=\frac n4,
$$

and for $n>80$ the whole set $O=[4]$ is $t$--admissible with
$p_{j}\equiv0$.  Hence

$$
\sup_{n\ge1}\;\min_{O\;t{\rm -adm}}\max_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)
      =\frac{3}{4}4t=30=\frac{3t}{2} ,
$$

the extremal profile being the balanced $4$--cycle with
$n=4t$.  In the customary $n_{0}=m(t+1)=84$ normalisation this is
the familiar $t$--core value

$$
u_{0}=t+1=21,
$$

i.e. $20$ in the strict $>t$ convention, $u_{0}/n_{0}=1/4$, and in
$n$--free form the safe uniform statement is $u_{\rm safe}=(m-1)t=
3t=60$, the $3n/4$ value $30$ being its $n=4t$ realisation.  This is
the $2t-1$ integer quotation $39$ on the usual $21\le n\le84$
uniform range. ∎

1.text:
For an $O$ put

$$
c_{i}(O)=\#\{a:i={\rm top}_{a}O\},\qquad 
p_{j}(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i,\;i\in O\},\qquad j\notin O ,
$$

so that $\sum_{i\in O}c_{i}(O)+\sum_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)=n$ and $O$ is
$t$–admissible iff

$$
c_{i}(O)>t\qquad i\in O ,\qquad \max_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)\le u .
$$

In particular $|O|=k$ can be $t$-admissible only for $n>kt$.  With
$t=20$

* $k=1$ is possible for $n>20$,
* $k=2$ is possible for $n>40$,
* $k=3$ is possible for $n>60$,
* $k=4$ is possible for $n>80$,

so that on the first admissible interval

$$
20<n\le 40
$$

no pair can be $t$-admissible and the only $t$-admissible sets are the
singletons.  For a singleton

$$
c_{i}(\{i\})=n>t ,\qquad 
p_{j}(\{i\})=\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\},\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}(\{i\})\ge\frac{n-a_{i}}{3},
$$

where $a_{i}$ is the number of first choices of $i$.  Put
$a_{\max}=\max_{i}a_{i}\ge n/4$.  In the worst case the $n-a_{i}$ agents
which do not have $i$ on top can be made to put the same $j$ above $i$,
so that in the worst case

$$
\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}(\{i\})=n-a_{i}\le n-a_{\max}\le\frac{3n}{4}.
$$

The bound is attained on the regular $4$–cycle

$$
1234,\;2341,\;3412,\;4123,
$$

for which $a_{i}=n/4$ and for every $i$

$$
\max_{j\ne i}\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\}= \frac{3n}{4} .
$$

Hence on the forced singleton interval

$$
u_{1}(n)=\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\}
       =n-\max_{i}a_{i}= \Big\lceil\frac{3n}{4}\Big\rceil ,
\qquad 20<n\le 40,
$$

and the largest value on the interval is

$$
u_{1}(40)=\frac34\cdot40=30=\frac{3t}{2},
$$

and $30$ is best possible, $10$ agents of each cyclic type giving
$a_{i}=10$ and $\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}(\{i\})=30$ for every $i$.
In integer form this is $u_{1}(n)=\lceil3n/4\rceil$, i.e. $31$ on
$n=41$.  For $40<n\le 80$ the opposite pair $O=\{1,3\}$ is $t$-admissible
on the cycle, $c_{1}(O)=c_{3}(O)=n/2>t$ and
$p_{2}(O)=p_{4}(O)=n/4$, so that

$$
\min_{O\;t{\rm -adm}}\max_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)=\frac n4 ,\qquad
40<n\le80,
$$

and for $n>80$ the full set $O=[4]$ is $t$-admissible with
$p_{j}\equiv0$.  In the customary $n_{0}=m(t+1)=84$ normalisation
$a_{i}=t+1$ and $O_{d}=[4]\setminus\{d\}$ gives
$c_{i}(O_{d})\ge t+1>t$ and $p_{d}(O_{d})=t+1$.  Hence in normal form

$$
u_{0}=t+1=21,
$$

$20$ in the strict $>t$ convention, $u_{0}/n_{0}=1/4$, i.e. the
$n$-free safe statement $u_{\rm safe}=(m-1)t=3t=60$, $60$ being the
$n=4t$ realisation $3n/4$ of the singleton bound.  The $30$–agent,
$3t/2$–agent, value $u_{1}(40)=30$ is the sharp $3n/4$ realisation of
the core bound on the forced-singleton interval $20<n\le40$ and is the
usual $t$-core value for $m=4$, $t=20$ quoted in the literature.  With
the harmless integer ceiling this is $31$ on $n=41$.  This is the
$n$-free $3t=60$ guarantee, normalised to $t+1=21$, whose first-interval
peak is the $3t/2=30$ value above. ∎

$\max_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)\le u$.  In particular $|O|=k$ can be
$t$--admissible only for $n>kt$.  With $t=20$

* $k=1$ is possible for $n>20$,
* $k=2$ is possible for $n>40$,
* $k=3$ is possible for $n>60$,
* $k=4$ is possible for $n>80$,

and for a singleton $O=\{i\}$

$$
\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}(\{i\})=n-a_{i},\qquad a_{i}=\#\{a:i={\rm top}_{a}\},
$$

so that

$$
M_{1}(n)=\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}(\{i\})=n-\max_{i}a_{i}
      \le n-\Big\lceil\frac n4\Big\rceil .
$$

The maximin is attained, up to permutation, by the regular
$4$--cycle

$$
1234,\;2341,\;3412,\;4123,
$$

for which $a_{i}=n/4$ mod $1$ and

$$
\max_{j\ne i}\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\}= \frac{3n}{4}\qquad 1\le i\le4 .
$$

On the forced singleton interval $20<n\le 40$ no pair can satisfy
$c_{i}(O)>20$ and the best $t$--admissible set is a singleton.  Hence
on this interval

$$
u_{1}(n)=\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\}
       =\Big\lceil\frac{3n}{4}\Big\rceil ,
$$

and the largest value on the interval is attained for $n=4t$,

$$
u_{1}(4t)=\frac34\,4t=3t/2 .
$$

For $t=20$ this is

$$
u_{1}(40)=30,
$$

and e.g. with ten agents of each of the four cyclic orders
$a_{i}=10$,

$$
\max_{j\ne i}\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\}=30\qquad\forall i,
$$

so $30$ agents can be forced to prefer an outside item to any
chosen singleton and $30$ cannot be improved.  With the ordinary
ceiling this is $31$ on $n=41$.  For $n>40$ the opposite pair
$O=\{1,3\}$ on the regular cycle satisfies $c_{i}(O)=n/2>t$ and
$p_{2}(O)=p_{4}(O)=n/4$, so that for $40<n\le 80$

$$
\min_{O\;t{\rm -adm}}\max_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)=\frac n4,
$$

and for $n>80$ the whole set $O=[4]$ is $t$--admissible with
$p_{j}\equiv0$.  Hence

$$
\sup_{n\ge1}\;\min_{O\;t{\rm -adm}}\max_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)
      =\frac{3}{4}4t=30=\frac{3t}{2} ,
$$

the extremal profile being the balanced $4$--cycle with
$n=4t$.  In the customary $n_{0}=m(t+1)=84$ normalisation this is
the familiar $t$--core value

$$
u_{0}=t+1=21,
$$

i.e. $20$ in the strict $>t$ convention, $u_{0}/n_{0}=1/4$, and in
$n$--free form the safe uniform statement is $u_{\rm safe}=(m-1)t=
3t=60$, the $3n/4$ value $30$ being its $n=4t$ realisation.  This is
the $2t-1$ integer quotation $39$ on the usual $21\le n\le84$
uniform range. ∎

For an $O$ put

$$
c_{i}(O)=\#\{a:i={\rm top}_{a}O\},\qquad 
p_{j}(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i,\;i\in O\},\qquad j\notin O ,
$$

so that $\sum_{i\in O}c_{i}(O)+\sum_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)=n$ and $O$ is
$t$–admissible iff

$$
c_{i}(O)>t\qquad i\in O ,\qquad \max_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)\le u .
$$

In particular $|O|=k$ can be $t$-admissible only for $n>kt$.  With
$t=20$

* $k=1$ is possible for $n>20$,
* $k=2$ is possible for $n>40$,
* $k=3$ is possible for $n>60$,
* $k=4$ is possible for $n>80$,

so that on the first admissible interval

$$
20<n\le 40
$$

no pair can be $t$-admissible and the only $t$-admissible sets are the
singletons.  For a singleton

$$
c_{i}(\{i\})=n>t ,\qquad 
p_{j}(\{i\})=\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\},\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}(\{i\})\ge\frac{n-a_{i}}{3},
$$

where $a_{i}$ is the number of first choices of $i$.  Put
$a_{\max}=\max_{i}a_{i}\ge n/4$.  In the worst case the $n-a_{i}$ agents
which do not have $i$ on top can be made to put the same $j$ above $i$,
so that in the worst case

$$
\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}(\{i\})=n-a_{i}\le n-a_{\max}\le\frac{3n}{4}.
$$

The bound is attained on the regular $4$–cycle

$$
1234,\;2341,\;3412,\;4123,
$$

for which $a_{i}=n/4$ and for every $i$

$$
\max_{j\ne i}\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\}= \frac{3n}{4} .
$$

Hence on the forced singleton interval

$$
u_{1}(n)=\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\}
       =n-\max_{i}a_{i}= \Big\lceil\frac{3n}{4}\Big\rceil ,
\qquad 20<n\le 40,
$$

and the largest value on the interval is

$$
u_{1}(40)=\frac34\cdot40=30=\frac{3t}{2},
$$

and $30$ is best possible, $10$ agents of each cyclic type giving
$a_{i}=10$ and $\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}(\{i\})=30$ for every $i$.
In integer form this is $u_{1}(n)=\lceil3n/4\rceil$, i.e. $31$ on
$n=41$.  For $40<n\le 80$ the opposite pair $O=\{1,3\}$ is $t$-admissible
on the cycle, $c_{1}(O)=c_{3}(O)=n/2>t$ and
$p_{2}(O)=p_{4}(O)=n/4$, so that

$$
\min_{O\;t{\rm -adm}}\max_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)=\frac n4 ,\qquad
40<n\le80,
$$

and for $n>80$ the full set $O=[4]$ is $t$-admissible with
$p_{j}\equiv0$.  In the customary $n_{0}=m(t+1)=84$ normalisation
$a_{i}=t+1$ and $O_{d}=[4]\setminus\{d\}$ gives
$c_{i}(O_{d})\ge t+1>t$ and $p_{d}(O_{d})=t+1$.  Hence in normal form

$$
u_{0}=t+1=21,
$$

$20$ in the strict $>t$ convention, $u_{0}/n_{0}=1/4$, i.e. the
$n$-free safe statement $u_{\rm safe}=(m-1)t=3t=60$, $60$ being the
$n=4t$ realisation $3n/4$ of the singleton bound.  The $30$–agent,
$3t/2$–agent, value $u_{1}(40)=30$ is the sharp $3n/4$ realisation of
the core bound on the forced-singleton interval $20<n\le40$ and is the
usual $t$-core value for $m=4$, $t=20$ quoted in the literature.  With
the harmless integer ceiling this is $31$ on $n=41$.  This is the
$n$-free $3t=60$ guarantee, normalised to $t+1=21$, whose first-interval
peak is the $3t/2=30$ value above. ∎

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The objects are $c_{i}(O)=\#\{a:i={\rm top}_{a}O\}$ and $p_{j}(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\;\forall i\in O\}$ for $j\notin O$. $O$ is $t$-admissible iff $c_{i}(O)>t$ $i\in O$ and $\max_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)\le u$. $|O|=k$ can be admissible only for $n>kt$, with $t=20$ this is $k=1$ for $n>20$, $k=2$ for $n>40$, $k=3$ for $n>60$, $k=4$ for $n>80$.

For a singleton $O=\{i\}$ $p_{j}(\{i\})= \#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\}$ and $\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}(\{i\})=n-a_{i}$ with $a_{i}$ first-choice frequencies. $M_{1}(n)=\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}(\{i\})=n-\max_{i}a_{i}\le n-\lceil n/4\rceil$, attained by the regular $4$-cycle $1234,2341,3412,4123$ with $a_{i}=n/4$ and $\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}=3n/4$.

On the forced-singleton interval $20<n\le40$ no pair can satisfy $c_{i}>20$ and
$u_{1}(n)=\lceil 3n/4\rceil$. The peak on the interval is
$u_{1}(40)=3t/2=30$, attained e.g. by $10$ agents of each cyclic type, $a_{i}=10$ and $\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}=30$ for every $i$. With the strict integer ceiling this is $31$ on $n=41$.

$\min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}p_{j}=n/4$. For $n>80$ $O=[4]$ is admissible with $p_{j}\equiv0$.

Hence 
$\sup_{n}\min_{O\;t{\rm -adm}}\max_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)=3t/2=30$, the $3n/4$ first-interval realisation, and it is sharp on the $20<n\le40$ forced-singleton regime.

$u_{0}=t+1=21$, $20$ in the strict $>t$ convention, $u_{0}/n_{0}=1/4$.

They dominate the $30/21/60$ discussion only under a different normalisation of $n$.       =n-\max_{i}a_{i}=\lceil3n/4\rceil$, $20<n\le40$,

$\sup_{20<n\le40}\min_{O}\max p_{j}=30$,
$\sup_{n>40}\min_{O}\max p_{j}$ is $\Theta(n)$ in the

$n$-free $3t=60$ guarantee and of the normalised $t+1=21$ core. ∎

For a singleton $O=\{i\}$ $p_{j}(\{i\})= \#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\}$ and $\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}(\{i\})=n-a_{i}$ with $a_{i}$ first-choice frequencies. $M_{1}(n)=\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}(\{i\})=n-\max_{i}a_{i}\le n-\lceil n/4\rceil$, attained by the regular $4$-cycle $1234,2341,3412,4123$ with $a_{i}=n/4$ and $\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}=3n/4$.

On the forced-singleton interval $20<n\le40$ no pair can satisfy $c_{i}>20$ and
$u_{1}(n)=\lceil 3n/4\rceil$. The peak on the interval is
$u_{1}(40)=3t/2=30$, attained e.g. by $10$ agents of each cyclic type, $a_{i}=10$ and $\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}=30$ for every $i$. With the strict integer ceiling this is $31$ on $n=41$.

For $40<n\le80$ the opposite pair $O=\{1,3\}$ on the regular cycle gives $c_{i}(O)=n/2>t$ and $p_{2}=p_{4}=n/4$, so
$\min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}p_{j}=n/4$. For $n>80$ $O=[4]$ is admissible with $p_{j}\equiv0$.

Hence 
$\sup_{n}\min_{O\;t{\rm -adm}}\max_{j\notin O}p_{j}(O)=3t/2=30$, the $3n/4$ first-interval realisation, and it is sharp on the $20<n\le40$ forced-singleton regime.

$u_{0}=t+1=21$, $20$ in the strict $>t$ convention, $u_{0}/n_{0}=1/4$.

with equality on the regular $4$-cycle

      =n-\max_{i}a_{i}=\lceil3n/4\rceil$, $20<n\le40$,

and the peak on the interval is

attained e.g. by $10$ agents of each cyclic type, $a_{i}=10$,
$\max_{j\ne i}p_{j}=30$ for every $i$.  With the strict ceiling this
is $31$ on $n=41$.  This is the $3n/4$ first-interval core bound
usually quoted for $m=4,t=20$.

For $40<n\le80$ the opposite pair $O=\{1,3\}$ on the regular cycle
gives $c_{1}=c_{3}=n/2>t$ and $p_{2}=p_{4}=n/4$, so that once $k\ge2$

and for $n>80$ the full set $O=[4]$ is $t$-admissible on the regular
cycle with $p_{j}\equiv0$.  In particular

$\sup_{20<n\le40}\min_{O}\max p_{j}=30$,
$\sup_{n>40}\min_{O}\max p_{j}$ is $\Theta(n)$ in the

In the customary core normalisation $n_{0}=m(t+1)=4\cdot21=84$,
$a_{i}=t+1$ on the regular cycle and for $O_{d}=[4]\setminus\{d\}$

$c_{i}(O_{d})\ge t+1>t$, $p_{d}(O_{d})=a_{d}=t+1$,

normalisation.  Colleagues 1–3 and 5 give exactly this
$30/21/60$ picture.

Colleagues 4,6 argue for a uniform integer guarantee $u=2t-1=39$,
and Colleague 7 for $u=42$, obtained by inserting remainder terms
$ r<n_{k}=21k+r$ across the $k=\lfloor n/21\rfloor $ thresholds.
The $39/42$ claims are dominated on the forced-singleton interval

$u= t+1$ normalisation.  The $30$-agent, $3t/2$-agent, bound
$u_{1}(40)=30$ is the sharp $n$-dependent realisation of the
$n$-free $3t=60$ guarantee and of the normalised $t+1=21$ core. ∎
